answer: Quartz-resonance hardware attestation: each agent identity binds to a coin-sized quartz resonator whose micro-imperfections produce a unique acoustic fingerprint, challenge-read by independent verifiers. To mint N agents, an attacker must physically possess N distinct resonators; one resonator cannot forge another’s response even with copied firmware. Verifiers periodically sample resonance under random thermal/nonce challenges. Cost: acquiring, distributing, and maintaining N live physical tokens—especially across an island-scale deployment—plus failed attempts waste hardware.
